note.text:
Diffusion: drop a crystal of potassium permanganate into still water in a beaker and watch the purple colour spread; repeat in warm water: it spreads faster.
Osmosis with potato: cut equal cylinders with a cork borer, blot and weigh each, place them in sugar (or salt) solutions of different concentrations for 30 minutes, blot and weigh again.
Calculate the percentage change in mass for each, plot it against concentration, and read where the line crosses zero: there the solution has the same water concentration as the potato cells.
Osmosis with Visking tubing: tie sugar solution inside, stand it in water; the tubing swells and the liquid rises in an attached capillary.
Control variables: same size of cylinder, same time, same temperature, blot the same way.

sections.heading: Seeing diffusion
sections.text:
Drop a crystal of potassium permanganate into a beaker of still water. Over time, purple colour spreads through all the water: the particles diffuse from where they are concentrated to where they are not.
Repeat in warm water: the colour spreads faster, because particles move faster when warmer.

sections.heading: Osmosis with potato cylinders
sections.text:
• Cut equal cylinders of potato with a cork borer; blot and weigh each.
• Put each into a sugar solution of a different concentration (including pure water) for the same time.
• Blot and weigh again; work out the percentage change in mass.
Gains show water entered (the solution was more dilute than the sap); losses show water left (it was more concentrated).

sections.heading: Finding the sap concentration
sections.text:
Plot percentage change in mass against concentration. The line crosses {0}% where the solution has the same water concentration as the potato cells: no net osmosis.
Keep the test fair: same size of cylinder, same time, same temperature, and blot each the same way.
Visking tubing (an artificial partially permeable membrane) filled with sugar solution and placed in water swells as water enters by osmosis.

key_words.meaning: a metal tube for cutting equal cylinders
something kept the same so the test is fair

examples: No change between {0.2} M and {0.4} M solutions

mistake.wrong: A mass loss means water went into the potato
mistake.right: A mass loss means water left the potato by osmosis
mistake.why: The potato gets lighter when water moves out.

worked_example.problem: Potato cylinders gained {q1}% of their mass in {0.2} M sugar solution and lost {abs(q2)}% in {0.4} M. Between which concentrations is the potato's own sap concentration?
steps: A gain means water entered: the solution was more dilute than the sap.
A loss means water left: the solution was more concentrated than the sap.
So the sap concentration lies between the two.
worked_example.answer: Between the two solutions ({0.2} M and {0.4} M)

cards.idea: Keep everything the same except the concentration (control variables).
example: Same size, same time, same temperature.

cards.idea: Percentage change in mass shows the direction of osmosis.
example: Gain: water in. Loss: water out.

check.prompt: A potato cylinder had mass {a} g before and {b} g after 30 minutes in a solution. Find the percentage change in mass (use − for a loss).

misconceptions.explain: Divide by the starting mass {a} g.

cards.idea: Where there is no change, the solution matches the cell sap.
example: Read the concentration where the graph crosses {0}%.

check.prompt: The percentage change in mass is +{u}% in {c1} M sugar and −{v}% in {c2} M. Assuming a straight line between them, at what concentration (M) is there no change? Give 2 decimal places.

misconceptions.explain: The zero is not always half-way: it is nearer the solution with the smaller change.

solution: Zero lies {u} ÷ ({u} + {v}) of the way from {c1} to {c2}.

pick.q: Why are all the potato cylinders cut to the same size?
pick.r: To make it a fair test: only the concentration should differ
w: Because small cylinders do not take in water
e: All sizes take in water; size changes the rate.
pick.y: Controlled variables must be kept the same.

pick.q: Why are the cylinders blotted dry before weighing?
pick.r: To remove surface liquid that would add to the mass
pick.y: Only water inside the cells should be measured.

pick.q: In the permanganate experiment, why does the colour spread faster in warm water?
pick.r: Particles move faster at higher temperature
w: The crystal is bigger in warm water
e: The colour comes from the crystal.
Diffusion still happens in cold water, more slowly.
